nodes.label: Package & Extension Manifest
nodes.rationale: Single manifest consumed by bootstrap scripts in .chezmoiscripts; scripts iterate these lists to install all tools and extensions from one authoritative source of truth

nodes.label: Windows Work-Laptop Apps
nodes.rationale: Optional work-laptop apps (DBeaver, Rancher Desktop, Codex, Copilot App) installed only when user answers yes to installWorkApps prompt at chezmoi init; defaults to yes on machines marked as work

nodes.label: Linux Cargo Packages
nodes.rationale: Cargo-installed packages supplement apt because gitui, git-delta, and eza are not reliably packaged in apt on all Linux distributions

nodes.label: Work vs Personal Machine Model
nodes.rationale: Nothing machine- or employer-specific is versioned. Identity, signing key, internal host/org URLs, safe.directory entries, and local repo paths belong in per-machine non-versioned ~/.config/git/config.local, which chezmoi seeds once from init prompts and never overwrites

nodes.label: OS-Divergent Config Strategy
nodes.rationale: OS-divergent configs (bat, gitui, VS Code) stored once under ~/.config; on Windows a run_onchange script links them into %APPDATA% using directory junctions for gitui and bat (live link, no admin required), while VS Code settings are copied because its User folder holds machine state that must not be redirected

nodes.label: Three-Tier Configuration System
nodes.rationale: Configuration merges in order: built-in defaults in Create.ps1 then global .defaults.json then task-specific task.config.json (highest priority last), so tasks only specify what differs from defaults, minimizing verbosity
